model_selection.why: Hard-negative miss rate is the primary axis for this project and is now a tie (1.19%-1.52% across candidates), so the old justification for shipping LinearSVC no longer holds. macro-F1 differences sit inside the seed spread; the choice is made on hard-negative miss rate, stability across grouped splits, and the absence of the word-n-gram false-scam failure mode.
model_selection.previous_choice_invalidated_because: its 24-point hard-negative advantage was caused by missing legitimate training data, not by the classifier. Closing that data gap removed the advantage entirely.

evaluation_note: The published score is indicative: 305 messages were labelled by one annotator, who also human-reviewed the 78 initial model disagreements. There is no second annotator or agreement statistic; the score remains against the original labels.
known_limitations: Tenglish and Hindi support is synthetic-only and unaudited by a native speaker.
Roughly 6% of the labelled corpus sits in a review queue and is excluded from training.
marketing_spam vs scam is a judgement boundary, not a crisp fact.
Validation accuracy on the pure-Devanagari and pure-Telugu slices is near chance. Those scripts have too few rows to support a per-language claim; see the ADEQUACY CHECK in the corpus build log.
macro-F1 differences between the top two candidate models are inside the seed spread, so the shipping choice rests on the hard-negative axis and on stability, not on macro-F1.
privacy: Message bodies are processed in memory and never written to disk or application logs.
